hypothesis: Treating click and long_view as ordinal feedback levels and training BPR on all valid pairs (long_view > no_click, long_view > click_only, click_only > no_click) will provide granular gradients for items and give all-negative users a ranking signal, raising primary.
rationale: The streak is at 2, requiring a guaranteed >+0.002 gain. We maintain the champion's proven features and 5-seed ensemble and introduce ordinal BPR pairs. By utilizing `is_click` as a secondary threshold (7s play time) beneath the primary `long_view` (18s), we unlock gradients for purely negative users and improve granularity without changing the model architecture.

lesson: Ordinal BPR on click and long_view pairs primary 0.5970 vs 0.6050, kept_champion.

harness_extra.gain_evidence: This directly targets the ~40% of users who have no long_views and are ignored by standard BPR, as well as providing intra-negative ranking for mixed users. The dataset mechanics confirm is_click and long_view are nested (7s vs 18s play time), mapping perfectly to ordinal decomposition. Prior runs failed with pointwise multi-task click, but incorporating ordinal pairs into BPR preserves the powerful pairwise ranking objective (+0.0115 historical gain) while strictly adding new valid signal.
harness_extra.ablation_plan: champion_equiv: exactly the champion baseline (train with only long_view pairs) to isolate the impact of the ordinal pairs.
